(i) the surface of ${\mathrm{MoS}}_{2}$ is stable in the presence of water, and that (ii) water is not able to stabilize a polar oxide termination of ${\mathrm{\alpha}}$-${\mathrm{RuCl}}_{3}$ in the absence of oxygen.

(i) a water-rich environment stabilizes a polar surface structure of ${\mathrm{Ruo}}_{2}(1\mathrm{10})$, (ii) this surface structure is stable at very low oxygen pressures, and (iii) the surface structure changes with the water vapor pressure.
the surface structure of ${\mathrm{Ruo}}_{2}(11 0)$ is very sensitive to water vapor and can be tuned over a wide range by varying the gas phase conditions.

the surface structure of the RuO2(100) surface is determined by a delicate balance of the oxygen partial pressure and water partial pressure.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of a humid atmosphere stabilizes a polar termination of ${\mathrm{TiO}}_{2}$ and ${\mathrm{ZrO}}_{2}$.

the polar termination is the thermodynamically stable structure for all experimentally accessible gas conditions, and the nonpolar termination is only stable in the presence of a high oxygen pressure.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a humid environment can stabilize an oxide termination that would not exist at the same temperature and pressure in a dry environment.
a humid environment can significantly change the surface structure of the oxide, which in turn can have important consequences on the chemical reactivity of the oxide.
